items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And my first thought was if I ever get to make a CD I’m going to ask him to play with me, which I did.

ctx.x: What inspired you to pursue your education all the way through a doctoral degree?

Well this is a — this will sound — it’s not lame but I mean I just wanted to move to New York. I didn’t have any thoughts like — I never even though about going to graduate school, when I was at SUNY Binghamton. There was a concert there with a bassist, Michael Moore was the bass player. And I love the way he played. And my first thought was if I ever get to make a CD I’m going to ask him to play with me, which I did. But I was saying to him, “I’m going to move to New York next year, any hints like what should I…

graduate scholarship.” And then I got my master’s degree and then they hired a new program director and the department started to get better. And then I was done and they said, “we don’t want you to go we’re going to give you a doctoral fellowship.” So when you don’t have any money or a job it’s hard to turn down free school and a little salary. So that’s maybe not the best, I didn’t have like high academic aspirations, so I mean that’s why I finished all my doctoral coursework and I’m embarrassed to say I was my…
